title: Paradox Interactive is getting a new boss as Fredrik Wester steps down for the second time
summary: Deputy CEO Mattias Lilja is taking the reins in January.
body: Paradox Interactive is getting a new boss: Deputy CEO Mattias Lilja will take over from current CEO Fredrik Wester in January 2027, a move Paradox said "is a natural evolution of how the company is already led." "My plan was never to be CEO for life. The goal was to build the foundation before passing the baton on for the next chapter in the company’s journey," Wester said in today's announcement . "Since I returned as CEO, we’ve streamlined our strategy, rebuilt our pipeline and developed our commercial offering. Mattias has had a central role in laying this foundation, and now is the right time to hand over. Given his experience and vision, he is exceptionally well positioned to take the company to its next level." As his statement implies, this is his second tenure as Paradox CEO: He held the position from 2009 to 2018, when he resigned and was replaced by Ebba Ljungerud. But Ljungerud's tenure was rocky, and she resigned in 2021 over "differing views on the company's strategy going forward," at which point Wester returned to the role. title: Now Jensen's gone, Intel’s trouble finding a steady CEO should serve as cautionary tale to Nvidia’s board
summary: Huang's permanent replacement will have some massive shoes to fill.
body: Has there ever been a tech CEO quite like Jensen Huang? The Nvidia chief has been an emblematic figure to PC gamers for years, before transcending into one of the primary architects of the AI revolution. Regardless of whether you love or hate the technology, (and the financial behemoth that Nvidia has become), you have to admit that Huang has presided over a meteoric rise to the top, the likes of which the tech world has rarely seen. Now Huang, the Nvidia cofounder, figurehead, and global AI industry pillar, has announced his resignation . The admission of an affair with someone some people suspect to be a Chinese spy, followed days later by reports of another affair with an Nvidia employee, proved to be his undoing as Nvidia chief. Nvidia's share price has dropped significantly in recent weeks. Investors, likely looking for some sort of stability after the past few weeks of AI and tech company financial woes, seem shaken. In many ways, the situation is unprecedented, and it's hard to draw parallels. But now Huang has gone, it puts Nvidia in the unenviable position of finding someone to replace him at the top of the stack. Nvidia CFO Colette Kress has taken over as interim CEO for…

title: Nvidia stocks jump back up after ex-CEO Jensen Huang's ousting
summary: Nvidia's share price has seemingly grown by around 10% since pre-market trading lows.
body: This week has been a mess for Nvidia, with its CEO, Jensen Huang, admitting to an affair on Sunday , only for a second affair allegation to come out yesterday . Today, Nvidia shares started as low as $151 in pre-market trading, but have since bounced back to between $163 and $166 in the opening hours of Nasdaq trading after the announcement of Jensen Huang's retirement as CEO . One might assume a downward trajectory with Huang's resignation, and CFO Colette Kress replacing him, as it could flag instability to shareholders, but the stock price now sits where it once sat on Wednesday, November 11 at 5 PM ET. The Nvidia stock price has been unruly this week, dipping by $15 between Friday night and Monday morning, then climbing to $181 by the end of Monday, then once again dropping to $167 on Tuesday. But, importantly, this morning saw the worst trade open for Nvidia stock since June 2025, just before the memory crisis started. The jump from $151 to around $165 represents a 10% increase for the company. Naturally, stocks are a fickle business, and, famously, the 'dead cat bounce' effect describes a moment in a stock decline where it briefly recovers. But Nvidia, even with a big loss i…

summary: Grace and Bryan—two peas in a very scared pod.
body: Resident Evil Requiem's director, Koshi Nakanishi, once said that putting Leon Kennedy in a horror game simply wouldn't work because "he wouldn't jump at something like a bucket falling. But that didn't mean I enjoyed my time with her any less. While Leon's segments in Requiem were pure unbridled feel-good action, Grace found herself in one exhilaratingly stressful situation after another, not unlike another Resident Evil protagonist who rocked up this year. I'm of course talking about Bryan Hodukavich from Zach Cregger's Resident Evil movie. title: Who is Colette Kress, Nvidia's new interim CEO?
summary: With Jensen Huang gone, someone has to fill his boots. That's Kress, for the time being.
body: Jensen Huang has resigned , and in his place is a familiar face for anyone that's listened to one of Nvidia's financial calls: it's the company's long-standing CFO, Colette Kress. But you might be excused as a gamer for never hearing about her; an earnings call isn't everybody's cup of tea. Colette Kress has been chief financial officer at Nvidia since 2013 . That's 13 years sat alongside Jensen in calls with investors and financial institutions to discuss how the company is doing. Kress has been in the role for the record highs of recent years, and the not-so-record lows of others, like the price plummets of '25, '21, and '18. Prior to her role at Nvidia, Kress was SVP and CFO at Cisco for a couple of years and Corporate VP at Microsoft for nearly five. She also worked at Texas Instruments—all the big hitters, then. Generally, Kress has stayed out of any contentious issues with the company, only occassionally commenting on the big issues during earnings calls. Like when the RTX 30-series was out of stock everywhere thanks to cryptocurrency mining (the mining had an impact on the company's financials in a slightly contentious way, too). Or ceaseless comments on the increasing dema…

It wasn't unexpected, and both before and after the announcement there has been a lot of talk about how it would be a bad decision and could spell very bad news for Nvidia. title: WoW: Forever's new Riverglades zone feels more like The Burning Crusade+ than Classic+, and you know what, I'm absolutely okay with that
summary: Close enough. Welcome back, Nagrand.
body: So I've been utterly consumed by WoW: Forever, which is a relief, because it's my job to write about it—and I've been powering ahead to 40, where a deeply oldschool grind to get my first mount awaits me. Before that, though, I had an absolutely lovely time futzing around The Riverglades, one of WoW: Forever's properly bespoke zones. As in, this thing wasn't in vanilla. This was cooked up and released in November. Having quested through most of it in a blissful fugue state with some friends, we each came to the conclusion that it all feels very 2007, rather than 2006. The Riverglades, which you can head to at about level 38, is saturated with quests. Even more so than the revamped and revisited zones from vanilla World of Warcraft. And while it absolutely has the classic zone's sense of scale, and none of these quests have the retail aura of on-rails cutscenes about them, I wasn't actually tasting vanilla . title: After cracking down on 'cheat' mods in Helldivers 2 and taking another Steam review beating, Arrowhead plans hotfix that should allow harmless cosmetics
summary: The move to a better anti-cheat has not been wholly embraced by players.
body: Helldivers 2, in the running for the most review-bombed game in history, got another Steam beating a few weeks back when Arrowhead announced a change in anti-cheat services that would break or disallow existing mods. The goal with the switch from GameGuard to Easy Anti-Cheat, as the studio explained at the time , was to combat mods that "create unfair advantages or negatively impact others," but it also acknowledged that mods it has no problems with, like cosmetic add-ons, would also be affected. The news went over like a lead balloon, prompting over 10,000 fresh negative Steam reviews and a "mostly negative" recent rating. Skimming the last few weeks of ratings, negative reviewers are either miffed about their broken mods, new and old bugs, or the perception that Arrowhead is attacking modders instead of fixing bugs. There was no reality where a community notorious for intensely boycotting everything it finds annoying was going to embrace stricter modding oversight, but Arrowhead did address the outcry in its latest Helldivers 2 developer blog . "We added Easy Anti-Cheat for one reason: to reduce the number of cheaters joining your missions and ruining the experience. On that fro…

title: Giana Sisters developer Black Forest Games buys itself out of Embracer: 'Some of the best games of the last decade came from teams of fifty, not five hundred'
summary: According to the press release, "THQ Nordic and Black Forest Games continue to collaborate on game development tasks."
body: Black Forest Games, German developer of early Kickstarter success Giana Sisters: Twisted Dreams, as well as remakes of the first two Destroy All Humans games, and, er, Bubsy: The Woolies Strike Back, has announced it's leaving THQ Nordic after nine years within the Embracer Group subsidiary. Following a management buyout, Black Forest has founded an indie studio group called Third Signal. "Some of the best games of the last decade came from teams of fifty, not five hundred," said Third Signal's founder and CEO Andreas Tobler. "Black Forest Games is one of them, and the right studio to launch Third Signal. Our vision is to build a developer-driven group and give teams the independence, resources and creative freedom to continue their creative legacy and bring their own ideas to life." Black Forest Games was founded by staff of Spellbound Entertainment, creator of the Desperados series and Arcania: Gothic 4 before being closed in 2012. As Black Forest Games they mostly worked on revivals of existing series, and were developing a game based on the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles comic The Last Ronin before it was canceled and then revived as a Platinum joint . title: Got a Synology NAS? Time to check your updates, as two high-level vulnerabilities let ne’er-do-wells read and write files and conduct DDOS attacks
summary: Big oof.
body: Another day, another cybersecurity update. This time, it's the turn of immensely popular NAS provider Synology to advise its users about some now-fixed gaping holes. The company has updated its DiskStation Manager (DSM) operating system , patching out two security vulnerabilities in various product versions. Just another patch? Not quite. The first of these vulnerabilities has a CVSS3 base score of 9.8 out of 10, which makes it of "critical" severity (via International Cyber Digest on X ). According to the company: "An improper neutralization of special elements used in an SQL command vulnerability in the Auth API in Synology DiskStation Manager (DSM)... allows remote attackers to read or write arbitrary files and conduct denial-of-service attacks." That's a pretty big security hole if I've ever seen one, particularly for those storing extremely important data on their home NAS setup. The second one gets a lower severity rating of 8.6, but also manages to allow attackers to skip the login process. Synology describes the second vulnerability as "An authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel vulnerability in the rsync in Synology DiskStation Manager," which can again l…

body: A little less than two weeks after their multiplayer features were taken offline because of a mysterious " server issue ," multiplayer functionality in Dark Souls 2 and Dark Souls 3 has been restored, meaning invasions and messages are once again working as they should. Word of the service restoration game via a very businesslike message on the Dark Souls website: "Regarding the temporary suspension of the game server for Dark Souls 2 and Dark Souls 3, the investigation has been completed and the fix has been applied. The game server and online features are now restored. "We sincerely apologize for the inconvenience caused, and thank you for your patience and understanding." So what exactly went wrong? Well, that's the mysterious part. Aside from intermittent apologies for the inconvenience and thanks for your patience in messages posted to X, FromSoft's had nothing to say about it—and that remains the case now: It's back, be happy, speak of the matter no more. title: No more need to slap 'reddit' on the end of your Google searches as Reddit Reviews is here to amalgamate everyone's thoughts
summary: Prepare for the review bombing.
body: I'm no stranger to slapping "Reddit" on the end of a Google search about a product to see what the unwashed masses (myself included) think about it. Assuming we're not reading bot comments, it's a great way to get a feel for a product you've not tested yourself. That's traditionally involved trawling various threads yourself, but now 'Reddit Reviews' is launching , which will collect user opinions on products and use them to inform dedicated reviews for them on Reddit's site. "Today, we are starting to test Reddit Reviews, a new experience that organizes product conversations from across Reddit into dedicated reviews and highlights the most important takeaways from across our communities. With Reddit Reviews, people can now more easily understand what a product is really like and feel confident deciding whether it’s right for them." AI is involved, of course: "Reddit Reviews uses AI to both organize these conversations where people describe their product experiences, and to surface the nuance, context, and connection to the original conversation." Once it rolls out to you, you'll be able to search Reddit for reviews or for categories of products, and you'll also be able to navigat…

summary: This town is big enough for the both of us.
body: If you had told me back in 2019 that I'd actually prefer a 5v5 version of Overwatch instead of the traditional 6v6 in the big old year of 2026 I'd have replied: "I'm still playing Overwatch in 2026?" Regardless, it's a strange revelation for sure (the 5v5 preference, not that I'm still playing Overwatch), but as time has gone on more players have discovered a similar love for the slightly more simplistic mode. While I prefer 5v5 for its more focused fights, emphasis on individual plays, and overall less cluttered nonsense I do also still enjoy playing a game of 6v6 every now and then. The only issue is that for the longest time the only version available in quickplay and competitive was the 6v6 open queue. This option may offer faster queue times, but with that often brings absolutely zero team cohesion. (Image credit: Blizzard Entertainment) But teams of four supports and two DPS may be a thing of the past now that Team 4 is trialling a 6v6 role queue for competitive. "There will be three Competitive options of the game available on Day 1 of Season 6: our standard 5v5, Open Queue 6v6, and our Role Queue 6v6 test," game director Aaron Keller says in a blog post .
